minor.issue: Root-level health endpoints exist on the backend (verified on http://localhost:8001) but are NOT exposed through the public ingress — only /api/* is routed to backend. This is fine for K8s pod-level liveness/readiness probes (which hit containerPort 8001 directly), but if any probe is configured at the ingress/service level using a root path, it will hit Expo and return HTML. Recommend confirming the deployment manifest probe path matches: use containerPort + path '/health' (pod-level) OR switch probe path to '/api/health' if it goes through the ingress.

rca_of_issue: Original deployment failure RCA: seed() in server.py was awaited synchronously in @app.on_event('startup'). On Atlas (production Mongo), seed performs ~10+ find_one + insert_one round-trips plus bcrypt(rounds=12) hashing for 4 demo users — easily 5-15s of latency before uvicorn can accept the first request. Kubernetes readiness/liveness probes have a default failureThreshold * periodSeconds typically 3-10s — startup exceeds it -> pod marked unhealthy -> restart -> infinite loop. The applied fix (a) wraps seed in asyncio.create_task so on_event returns immediately and uvicorn starts accepting requests, (b) wraps seed in try/except so an Atlas connection failure logs but does not crash, (c) adds /api/health + /health endpoints that return {status:'ok'} without touching the DB so probes succeed even during/before seed runs. Verified all 3 mitigations work as expected in this sandbox.
